claims.statement: Activity islands share a 28-point collapsed height, minimum 72-point content width on an 8-point grid, at least 208-point compact width on a 16-point grid, and at least 288-point expanded width on a 32-point grid.
Activity-island width and height use one 240 ms cubic ease-out transition, preserving the visible size on reversal and applying target geometry directly for reduced motion.
Work and Debug preserve resting inner edges while one expands outward; a single activity is centered, and available space selects expanded, compact or minimum presentation.

Activity content keeps a fixed drawable at the native window origin with a sibling rounded mask; details retain their full-width layout, and secondary header fields appear only after they fit beside the persistent main value.

Conversation spacing uses 20 points between messages and around the 24-point work status, and 6 points between a completed process header and its answer; the composer contributes 8 points to the lower gap.

The composer uses a theme-accent Ultrafast glyph, shows an em dash for an explicitly unavailable model catalog, wraps suggestions in the normal editor, and reserves quotes for new conversations without history.

The automated native activity probe runs 20 Work and Debug transitions with four interrupted openings, checks foreground origin and viewport geometry, and requires no daemon or model request; its trace measures CPU draw and submission rather than GPU completion or scanout.
Repository instructions require all activity islands to reuse the shared geometry and motion contract and require new variants to update that contract and its focused checks.

A confirmed-empty personal Assistant topic shows the centered 20-point heading What’s next? and the same-Assistant explanation; a new project Agent shows What would you like to do? and its project chooser.

The shared empty-conversation start heading yields to saved history, sending previews, retained failed or unconfirmed input, active work, questions, and misalignment; missing or unavailable history retains its existing loading or retry presentation.

A missing selected working directory is presented as an unavailable working folder with a restoration instruction; generic connection admission failures use Reconnecting to Codex while account readiness failures keep their specific Accounts guidance.

The isolated native stream recovery test drops the first local SSE response before completion and proves that retry preserves the original running thread and turn, completes normally, and does not enqueue a duplicate input.

The left sidebar uses one 28-point row rhythm with no inter-section gap, 11-point muted section labels, 12-point project names, 12.5-point conversation text and 5-point row corners; only the two divider slots add 12 points.
Human attention is derived from pending native requests, unanswered native questions and explicit user-decision state rather than displayed labels; ordinary returned agent work is separate.
Window controls retain fixed-size icons without visible toolbar labels; Collaboration shows pending count in a small badge while keeping its name in the tooltip and accessibility label.

Conversation rows reveal fixed trailing Pin, Archive and Delete symbols; the first Delete click arms the same symbol with a red nudge, the second confirms, and Escape or an outside click cancels without changing the selected conversation or its draft.

The compact sidebar retains a 40-point rail, section symbols, conversation initials and a fixed command entry. A 100 ms hover expands it temporarily when the right panel is not floating; departure waits 220 ms, reentry cancels departure, and disclosure does not pin it.

Overflowing sidebar titles use hover or keyboard-focus motion by default, each section can opt into continuous scrolling, and leaving the hover returns the label through the shared tween with reduced-motion support.
The sidebar owner/time tooltip anchors eight points outside the row's trailing edge at the row top through GPUI's window-fitting anchored element, keeping the action hit targets uncovered.

During sidebar opening, closing and reversal, the content retains the complete expanded width and stays mounted while the outer panel clips its shared width transition; the settled 40-point rail omits project branches and trailing controls.

HoverIntent owns shared 100 ms entry dwell and 220 ms departure grace for the sidebar, activity islands and response-statistics popover; brief crossings cancel entry, internal movement keeps the original dwell, reentry cancels close, stale exits do not cancel a newer target, and explicit actions cancel pending hover work.

Committed hover intent and explicit surface toggles grant a bounded 400 ms animation window in a visible inactive App without changing the background-rendering preference; ordinary background policy resumes after expiry, and system reduced motion and VoiceOver still suppress motion.

Sidebar text retains its complete shaping, text, color and position behind a shared Viewport mask measured from actual pane bounds. The visible edge reveals or covers it without a per-label fade, character counter or reveal clock, while section symbols and conversation initials remain fixed.

The main macOS window leaves traffic_light_position unset and uses an AppKit unified compact toolbar; GPUI places its top control groups at the measured native control-row center instead of moving native window buttons or their containers.

Control groups share the 28-point height, 24-point targets, 4-point inner spacing and gap, 8-point outer inset and capsule radius, and 5-point small-control radius; attached material surfaces preserve their allocated anchor, while independent floating menus use the shared 8-point edge clearance.
Work and Debug headers reserve a 14-point waveform or performance-gauge symbol plus a 6-point gap, include that slot in measured sizing, and tint the symbols with the active accent color.

The main window minimum is 480 by 360 points. Panel allocation reserves 360 points for reading, retains the first-opened fitting panel, floats the other without shrinking conversation width, restores requested panels when space returns, and shows only the active temporary panel when neither fits.

Both workspace panels use one MaterialSurface host with PanelStyle::Workspace and Window material/glass style in docked, floating and compact navigation states. They retain native transparency and full-canvas clipping without extra workspace tint. Shortcuts target the main workspace, Escape dismisses temporary panels before reply interruption, and composer clipping retains the editor.

Work in progress projects unfinished tasks and observed native agents from the current conversation subtree when Graph is hidden; it reuses disclosure motion, opens existing conversations, and constrains its scrolling list to one quarter of window height between two and six 28-point rows.
Panel placement state comes from open workspace allocation and remains docked or floating through closing and reversal; it governs allocation and dismissal without selecting a different material.

When Overlay glass style has no saved override it inherits Window glass style, including later changes, while an explicit Regular or Clear choice remains independent and inheritance creates no stored override.

workspace_panel_content supplies a shared system font, 12.5-point body size and 19-point line height without a background fill. Workspace panels keep their clipping transition and omit native menu opacity and vertical entrance effects.
The native sidebar owns pointer departure in expanded and compact states; the parent does not treat the native foreground as a pointer exit.

Workspace panels retain the same native host across width and placement changes until their visible width reaches zero. The compact left rail stays mounted. Parent-owned reveal geometry and retained presentations rendered through ui_layout::panel keep sidebar layout, SVG symbols and hover updates on the native foreground.
